notify_candidate_reads_subject_with_fall.detail: Line 116 changed to `@channel_message.subject.presence || "#{@job.title} at #{@organization.name}"`. Correctly reads the stored subject and falls back to the existing hardcoded literal when blank.

fallback_uses_presence.detail: .presence is used, which returns nil for nil, empty string, and whitespace-only strings. Correct per spec.

xss_in_subject_via_mailgun_api.detail: Traced the full path: subject string -> Emails::SendTemplateEmail#add_subject -> MessageBuilder#subject -> set_multi_simple(:subject, value) -> Mailgun REST API 'subject' parameter. The Subject: email header is rendered as plain text by all email clients, not as HTML. HTML tags in a subject line are displayed literally. Furthermore, outbound user-composed subjects are sanitized at the controller layer (Sanitizer#sanitize in ChannelMessagesController and BulkChannelMessagesController). Inbound subjects from Postmark are raw email Subject headers which are inherently plain text per email protocol (RFC 5322 does not allow HTML in Subject).

other_mailer_methods_needing_subject.detail: Only two active methods in ChannelMessageMailer: notify_team (phase 1b, correctly unchanged) and notify_candidate (correctly updated). The commented-out candidate_confirmation method is dead code.

clean_incoming_message_touches_subject.detail: clean_incoming_message (before_create callback) only processes body and body_sanitized_html. No changes to this method in the diff. Subject is a plain string that does not need the body-cleaning pipeline (which handles HTML email body parsing). Correct per spec.

anonymization_nil_safety.detail: Traced text_replacer in CandidatesController: it guards with `return text if text.blank?`, so nil subject on legacy channel_messages passes through safely as nil.
